title: Ethena capital charges depend on the path of exposure, penalizing collateral risk that is uncorrelated with the asset lent
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 splits Ethena Exposures into three kinds — Direct (holding USDe/sUSDe), Indirect (lending against Ethena-related assets through lending markets), and Pendle (holding PT-USDe/PT-sUSDe) — and assigns each its own Instance Financial CRR. Two of the Indirect cases are worth putting side by side:

- **Lending Ethena-related assets against Ethena-related collateral** (e.g. USDe against PT-USDe): **3%** (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2.1)
- **Lending non-Ethena-related assets against Ethena-related collateral** (e.g. USDC against PT-USDe): **4%** (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2.2)

The same underlying counterparty risk, the same collateral, but the position lending *dollars* against it requires a third more capital than the position lending *USDe* against it.

The reasoning is correlation. If USDe depegs, a lender who supplied USDe holds a claim denominated in the same impaired unit — its liability shrinks alongside its collateral. A lender who supplied USDC holds a hard claim against collateral that just fell, and absorbs the full gap. Matched exposure is self-hedging in a way unmatched exposure is not, so the capital charge tracks the mismatch rather than the asset.

The partial-look-through rule makes this operational: "only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena related assets is subject to" the Ethena CRR, with the rest "calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure." A capital requirement is therefore a weighted blend over a lending market's *collateral composition*, not a property of the market an Agent deposited into — which means the requirement moves when other users of that market change their collateral, with no action by the Agent.
description: Directly holding USDe or lending Ethena assets against Ethena collateral costs 3%; lending USDC against PT-USDe collateral costs 4%, because the lender's asset does not move with the collateral.
